newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call rates dip, but seen recovering Friday.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call rates dip, but seen recovering Friday.

text.p: Dutch call money fell six basis points to 2.75 percent bid on Thursday on the back of an ample special advances allocation, but were seen picking up again when tax payments fall due on Friday.
"The allocation was quite generous and pushed overnight rates down," one dealer said.

The Dutch central bank said it allocated 6.47 billion guilders to the money market under an eight-day pact at an unchanged rate of 2.50 percent. The pact replaces a 3.74 billion six-day allocation expiring today, which had been seen as tight.
But Thursday's dip was seen as temporary.
Dealers said call would pick up again on Friday as end-of-month tax payments and weekend money requirements squeezed liquidity.
"Looking at rates over the weekend, you can easily conclude that call will go up again," one dealer said.
One-month rates were unchanged from yesterday, as were the other money market rates.
The guilder was virtually unchanged against the mark at 112.21 per 100 marks versus 112.20 on Wednesday. Guilder/mark rates were not affecting the money market, dealers said.
